clue.text: Obstructing outside right and getting the edge

indicators.note: outside says the word for obstructing goes around the letter for right

parts.note: obstructing means stopping

explanation.surface: A player blocking an opponent on the right wing and gaining an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: To strop a razor is to sharpen it on a leather strap, so the definition is about putting an edge on a blade, not gaining an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stropping a razor on leather hones its blade, giving it a keen cutting side.

clue.text: Americans in the Senate?

parts.note: the Senate seats two people for each US state, so its members can be read as men of the states

explanation.surface: A question about US senators.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior politicians are called by this title, and senators represent states, so the split reading fits them twice over.

clue.text: Didn't walk round a show.

parts.note: someone who did not walk may have ridden, past tense rode
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone who skipped walking took a ride round an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a preposition, but it supplies the ring-shaped letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of bronco riding and roping is a public spectacle staged for an audience.

clue.text: Being there, coppers outside rescue half the characters

indicators.note: outside says the word for coppers wraps around the letters from rescue

parts.note: coppers are low-value bronze coins, pence

indicators.note: half the characters means the first three of the six letters of rescue

explanation.surface: Police are present at the scene of a rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means small coins: PENCE goes around RES, the first half of 'rescue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance at a place, the state of being in it, is a synonym.

clue.text: An example of the well-favoured position

parts.note: something well favoured is popular or fashionable, which is in
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A sample of a favourable posture.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point or illustration is a synonym for one example.

clue.text: A pleasant place for fish study

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Somewhere nice to study fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivated plot of flowers and lawns is an agreeable spot, as in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Record set by female animal

indicators.note: set by says the record word is placed beside the female word, after it

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A disc made by a woman about a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly farm creature kept for its fleece is one example of a beast.

clue.text: Top decoration presented in a case

indicators.note: presented in says the decoration letters are put inside the case word

parts.note: a suit is a case in law, a lawsuit
MM is the Military Medal, a decoration for bravery

explanation.surface: A ornament displayed at the top of a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a case' is a lawsuit, SUIT, which takes MM (Military Medal) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a mountain is its peak, the uppermost part.

clue.text: At .one time, a pit-worker's union had inspectors

parts.note: ex means former, at one time
a pit-worker is a coal miner; the possessive gives miner's

explanation.surface: Long ago a coal miners' union employed inspectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' signals that the pieces are joined together; the possessive apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People who test or scrutinise candidates or work are checkers of it, inspectors.

clue.text: A cupboard for papers

explanation.surface: A cabinet for storing newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a large cupboard for linen in older usage; the press also means newspapers collectively.

clue.text: Short notice to prepare a sermon

parts.note: ad is a short form of advertisement, a notice
to dress is to prepare, as with food or a wound

explanation.surface: A brief notice asks someone to get ready to preach.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech to a congregation or audience is one sense of the word.

clue.text: The odd wizard would make a search

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: A strange sorcerer would go hunting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM here is the British informal adjective for strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things untidily, to look for something.

clue.text: To call up is all right in the latter part of the day

indicators.note: in says the letters for all right go inside the word for evening

parts.words: the latter part of the day
parts.note: eve is a poetic word for evening
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Telephoning someone is fine in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up a memory or feeling is to bring it to mind, recall it.

clue.text: If spare it may be served as pre-dinner drinks

indicators.note: served suggests the letters are dished up in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: If there is any extra, it could be offered as cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be served' rearranges IF SPARE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers in liquid form, taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite, are such drinks.

clue.text: Golden and firm in imitation of grouse

indicators.note: in says the colour and company letters sit inside the word for imitation

parts.note: mock means imitation, as in mock leather
or is the heraldic word for gold
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Golden and solid like a fake game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like a complaint but is the game bird; OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: The male red grouse is called by this name, a moor bird of the heather.

clue.text: The invader got shot or otherwise dealt with

indicators.note: otherwise dealt with says these letters are handled in another order

explanation.surface: An attacker was shot or else handled some other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise dealt with' rearranges GOT SHOT OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The eastern Goths invaded the Roman Empire and founded a kingdom in Italy.

clue.text: The fare offered is some game, nuts and coffee

definitions.text: The fare offered is some game, nuts and coffee

indicators.note: some says only part of the words game and nuts is taken

explanation.surface: A restaurant's offerings: game, nuts and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes letters from inside 'game, nuts'; the whole clue describes a bill of fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of dishes on offer, here game, nuts and coffee, is a bill of fare.

clue.text: Clothing seen on a river-bed?

parts.note: the bed of a river lies beneath the River Wear in north-east England, so it is literally under it

explanation.surface: Garments found lying on the bottom of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in County Durham, England; garments worn beneath others split as 'under Wear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn beneath outer clothes, like pants and vests, are this.

clue.text: Drink with people in competition

parts.note: sack is an old word for sherry or white wine
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Having a drink with others during a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is the old fortified wine Falstaff loved; the answer is the children's sports-day event of hopping in bags.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day contest where runners jump along inside bags is a type of contest.

clue.text: Arranging a cut covering credit notes — prudent, that

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering puts the anagram above the credit letters
arranging says the letters of a cut are put in a new order

parts.note: IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt, credit notes

explanation.surface: Setting a cut over debts acknowledged is a careful move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' rearranges A CUT into CAUT, which sits above IOUS in this down entry, so 'covering' means on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful and wary of risk is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: A minute mark

explanation.surface: A tiny mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a written memo; to mark something is to notice it, both senses of the word.

clue.text: The blockhead rushed around, being annoyed

indicators.note: around says the word for rushed goes round the word for blockhead

parts.note: hared means ran fast, rushed
an ass is a fool, a blockhead

explanation.surface: The fool dashed about in a state of irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pestered and tormented is the state of the word, persistently troubled.

clue.text: Writer making points about copy

indicators.note: about says the compass points go round the word for copy

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: An author making remarks about plagiarism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' looks like remarks, but gives two compass letters, S and E, around CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk or copyist who writes documents by hand is a writer.

clue.text: Leave the area with insufficient 25

explanation.surface: Abandon the arid zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is the answer to 25-down, WATER, so the second definition is an arid region.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave; an arid region lacking rainfall is the noun sense.

clue.text: Rash investigation?

parts.note: a rash may be read as a skin outbreak of spots, so examining it is a look at the spots

explanation.surface: A hasty inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' seems to mean hasty, but read as a skin rash it is a check on the spots; the real sense is a random inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A random, on-the-spot inspection is the sense, punned on examining spots.

clue.text: It might well have gone to an old soldier's head

definitions.text: It might well have gone to an old soldier's head

parts.words: It might well have gone to an old soldier's head
parts.note: a phrase for something intoxicating, read literally as headgear placed on a past soldier

explanation.surface: Something that made a veteran giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to his head' suggests drink or pride, but the answer is literally worn on the head: a tall military cap with a peak and plume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical peaked military cap worn by soldiers in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Ancient building that has pull with royalty

parts.note: to tow is to pull
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An old structure with royal influence, like the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; the Tower of London is the royal fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall old structure such as a keep or fortress is the answer.

clue.text: In which Keats wrote his name

definitions.text: In which Keats wrote his name

parts.words: In which Keats wrote his name
parts.note: refers to the poet's chosen epitaph, Here lies one whose name was writ in an element that leaves no trace

explanation.surface: The medium a poet used for his signature.
explanation.walkthrough: John Keats asked for his gravestone to read 'Here lies One Whose Name was writ in Water'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's epitaph says his name was written in this liquid, meaning it would not last.

clue.text: :Produced a notice to indicate poison

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters of a notice are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A notice was put up to warn of a toxic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' rearranges A NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood or wolfsbane, a plant yielding a deadly toxin, is the answer.

clue.text: One of a dozen given a job by the French

parts.note: a post is a job
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone among twelve given work by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve disciples of Jesus are known by this title.

clue.text: Church in stone of a rich yellow colour

indicators.note: in says the church letters go inside the stone word

parts.note: ore is metal-bearing stone

explanation.surface: A church built of golden stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth pigment of yellow-brown shade is the answer.

clue.text: More secure after the change of rate is made official

indicators.note: after says the comparative comes after the rearranged rate
the change of says the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more secure

explanation.surface: The figure was safer after the interest rate changed, it was announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the change of' rearranges RATE into TREA, and SURER follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer in charge of a society's funds holds this post, an official.
